tob-10803: Magnus Maclean’s history traces Celtic literature from the ancient bards of Ireland and Wales through the medieval sagas to modern writers. He shows how a single poetic tradition survived conquest, famine, and the loss of its languages. The book offers a sweeping view of a literature that gave Europe the Arthurian legends and much else.
tob-13503: The Lesser Key of Solomon is the most famous grimoire — a manual of ceremonial magic — in Western history. Its first section, the Goetia, lists seventy-two demons with their seals and the rites for summoning and commanding them. This edition by the Chicago occult publisher L. W. de Laurence spread the text widely in early twentieth-century America.
tob-3003: The oldest surviving epic of the English language, made by an unknown Anglo-Saxon poet over a thousand years ago. It tells of the hero Beowulf, who slays the monster Grendel, Grendel’s vengeful mother, and at last a dragon — dying in the final fight. The poem’s brooding tale of courage and doom remains the crown of Old English writing.
tob-4003: Sir Thomas More’s 1516 dialogue pictures an island nation where goods are shared, work is capped at six hours, and gold is used for chamber pots. Written partly as a jab at England, it gave the world a new word: utopia. The book founded a whole line of made-up societies, from science fiction to political theory.
tob-14503: Rodwell’s Koran sets Islam’s writ in the order it came down, so English readers may track the message as it reached Muhammad — from early Meccan warnings to Medinan law. His 1861 version first tried this ordering in English. A hundred years it served readers.
tob-0003: The Vedas are Hinduism’s oldest writ — hymns, rites, and deep guessings set down in Sanskrit above three thousand years ago. The Rig Veda’s thousand hymns sing gods of sky, fire, and storm. These books are the headwaters of Indian faith and thought.
tob-0103: Abramelin’s second book gives the working part — the letter-squares, the names of spirits fair and foul, and the rites to rule them. It is the wonder-book’s beating heart. Wonder-workers for generations have pored over these pages, for weal or woe.
tob-4203: F. W. Burger’s Janus book tracks the two-faced god through Roman life and worship — his fanes, his rites, his seat at every beginning. The work musters the olden witness on Rome’s most home-grown godhead. It lights up the Roman holy mind. A sound piece of classic scholarship.
tob-9803: Thornley’s Englishing of Longus’s Daphnis and Chloe gives the olden Greek herd-tale — the stainless love of two foundlings herd-bred on Lesbos. The tale has gladdened readers two thousand years. Goethe loved it, and Ravel set it to music. This printing bears its mild fairness to English readers.
cia-0000119203: An August 1968 report comparing an unidentified POW photograph, number 109, with photos of Mr. Roy F. Townley. Photo comparison was painstaking MIA work — matching a face in a propaganda image to a missing man. The entry shows the forensic patience of the search for the missing.
cia-0000119703: A September 1952 estimate of probable developments in the Union of South Africa. Apartheid was being built into law, and the world was beginning to react. The document shows American analysts forecasting the future of a regime whose racism would define it for decades.
cia-0000124303: A November 1962 study determining the sizes of Cosmos-series satellites from mass-to-area ratios and brightness data — compared against American satellites. Photometry as espionage: judging a satellite's size by how it caught the light. The document is ingenuity in action — measuring the unreachable.
cia-0000132203: Situation Report 520: Israelis fearing Iraqi chemical attacks were imminent — the truncated title suggests the rest. Gas masks were distributed; sealed rooms prepared. The document captures the dread of a nation waiting for warheads that, mercifully, never came.
cia-0000132403: An estimated January 1961 document on Cuba and Latin America — the truncated title cuts off the focus. Three months before the Bay of Pigs, the Cuba file was thickening. The entry is the prelude to disaster: the invasion, being planned.
cia-0000132503: A February 1961 report on dissension in Ecuador over policy toward Cuba. Quito's government was torn — recognize Havana or shun it? The document is a small country's big dilemma: the Cuba question, dividing a nation.
cia-0000133203: An estimated 1961 untitled document: 83 photographs identified as JMTIDE — the truncated title cuts off the rest. JMTIDE was a cryptonym, the CIA's code for something. The entry is the code: the photos, labeled — the meaning, classified.
cia-0000137003: A 1954 cable on the extradition of asylees — the archive's spelling says asiles. The sheltering embassies' guests, to be handed over. The document is the demand: the extradition, sought — through a typo.
cia-0000140403: A 1952 I&I memo discussing an unnamed psychologist known for his work in hypnosis — the archive's punctuation stumbles. The expert, unnamed. The entry is the memo: the psychologist, discussed.
un-ga-res-303: Resolution 303 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1947. The second session's work. The catalog holds the number and year; the text holds the decision.
un-sc-res-103: Security Council Resolution 103, adopted in 1953. The deliberations continued. The number and year endure; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-203: Security Council Resolution 203, adopted in 1965. The deliberations rolled on. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1203: Security Council Resolution 1203, adopted in October 1998 — the Kosovo verification resolution, endorsing the OSCE verification mission and NATO air surveillance over Kosovo. The Council tried watching instead of warring — for a season. The resolution is the watch: the province, monitored.
un-sc-res-1403: Security Council Resolution 1403, adopted in 2002 — aligned. The Council deciding. The designation and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1903: Security Council Resolution 1903, adopted in 2009 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-2003: Security Council Resolution 2003, cataloged with the year 2000 — the numbering suggests 2011, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
cia-0000136703: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136703, the archive's date uncertain. The roughly dated papers. The entry is the roughness: the dating, soft.
plos-pone-0000003: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper on the invasion and persistence of a selfish gene in Cnidaria — the group including jellyfish and corals. Selfish genes spread by cheating inheritance, and this one conquered ancient animals. The paper is the invasion: the cheater gene, triumphant.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d103: President Roosevelt to Generalissimo Chiang, November 8, 1943 — Document 103. The same day, a letter to China's leader. The message is the parallel: two leaders, one day.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d203: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, November 10, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 203. Washington to London. The message is the correspondence: the president, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d303: The Secretary of State to the President, November 24, 1943 — Document 303. A second that day. The memo is the doubling: the day, crowded.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d403: The minister in Egypt, Kirk, to the president's special assistant Hopkins — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 403. Cairo wrote the insider. The cable is the insider's: Kirk, to Hopkins.
mysteries-of-paris-volume-03: Eugène Sue's sensational serial gripped all of France in the 1840s, and this volume continues the saga. Prince Rodolphe, disguised as a workman, moves through the Paris underworld — rescuing the innocent, punishing villains, and uncovering secrets. The book's huge success invented the urban mystery genre and made Sue the most-read novelist of his day.
the-thirty-years-war-volume-03: Volume three centers on the dramatic years of Wallenstein's ascendancy and Gustavus Adolphus's intervention — the war's most brilliant and terrible phase. Schiller, himself a dramatist, gives these larger-than-life figures their full Shakespearean stature. History at its most gripping.
history-of-the-revolt-of-the-netherlands: The third volume follows the Dutch struggle through its heroic middle years, as the Sea Beggars defy Spain and the northern provinces hold firm. Schiller celebrates the birth of a free republic in prose worthy of his subject. A stirring chapter in the history of liberty.
voyages-of-samuel-de-champlain-volume-03: The third volume of Champlain's journals covers his later explorations and the consolidation of French power in Canada. Wars with the Iroquois, the hardships of settlement, and Champlain's statesmanship fill these pages. The essential record of New France's founding father.
equality-pg7303: Edward Bellamy's follow-up to Looking Backward takes Julian West deeper into the year 2000 — its work, its play, its plain living. Less famed than the first book, it rounds out his dream of a fair world. A key work of old American socialist hope.
arxiv-2605-08803: Transfer operators describe how densities evolve under a dynamical system, and self-consistent versions let the evolution feed back on itself. Wael Bahsoun, Gary Froyland, and Maxence Phalempin approximate their fixed points with Newton's method, the classic root-finding workhorse. The 2026 paper is numerical analysis for chaotic dynamics.
arxiv-2605-09303: Diffusion language models generate text by denoising, but sometimes the word order collapses mid-generation. Jeonseong Kim explains it as path-dependent denoising, offering a non-conservative field perspective on order collapse. The 2026 paper is theory for the new breed of diffusion LLMs.
arxiv-2605-09503: Quantizing diffusion models group by group leaves uneven errors — some channels suffer far more than others. Yongsen Cheng, Kai Liu, Kaiwen Tao, and colleagues reorder channels to lower the per-group quantization error with PermuQuant. The 2026 paper squeezes diffusion models smaller and more evenly.
arxiv-2605-09603: Masked diffusion language models generate text in parallel — blazing fast but rough around the edges. Houxing Ren, Mingjie Zhan, Zimu Lu, and colleagues refine the draft output with edit-based refinement passes. The 2026 paper polishes parallel generation into something worth reading.
arxiv-2605-09703: Reading minds — inferring mental states — zero-shot, from real-world data, with multiple agents. Xiaoyu Yuan, Niklas Heikkala, Tiina Törmänen, and colleagues build MOTOR-Bench for the task. The 2026 paper is theory-of-mind AI with a benchmark.
arxiv-2605-09803: Smartphones remain hostile to blind and visually impaired users; LLMs could narrate the screen intelligently. Joshua Owusu Ansah, Anuj Kapoor, Ayush Khanna, and colleagues enhance mobile accessibility with their Insight system. The 2026 paper is assistive technology powered by language models.
arxiv-2605-10003: Bargmann invariants detect quantum coherence; a low-order hierarchy extends them to set coherence. Yan-Ling Wang develops the invariant hierarchy carefully. The 2026 paper is quantum information on coherence, ordered low to high. It orders coherence precisely and completely by invariant rank.
plos-pone-0003403: Public-health researchers surveyed antimalarial drug quality across Tanzania in this 2008 paper. Teams bought malaria medicines from retail shops nationwide and tested what was actually in the pills. The nationwide snapshot revealed how often patients receive substandard or fake drugs, a direct threat to malaria control in one of the hardest-hit countries.
plos-pone-0003503: Vision scientists caught the brain sorting sights in a flash in this 2008 study. By flipping images upside down, a trick that disrupts face and object processing differently, they found category-specific brain activity within the first 100 milliseconds. The result overturns the old view that early vision treats all complex scenes the same before sorting begins.
plos-pone-0003603: Neurovirologists found a genetic shield for the brain in this 2008 SIV study. A particular MHC class I allele protected infected macaques against lentiviral brain disease, a model for HIV's neurological toll. The neuroprotective allele suggests host genetics can specifically guard the central nervous system.
plos-pone-0003703: In 2008, Tito, Macmil, and Wiley read the gut bugs of ancient humans. Phylotyping two old microbiomes, they mapped which microbes lived in people long ago and what jobs those microbes did. The ancient census sets a baseline for how modern guts, and their ills, have changed.
plos-pone-0003803: Chua, Voon, and Crameri introduced a new respiratory virus in this 2008 paper. The novel orthoreovirus, isolated from patients with acute respiratory infections, expands a family once thought harmless. The characterization puts a new suspect on the board for unexplained breathing illness.
plos-pone-0003903: Back in 2008, Rao, Burley, and Swaminathan solved structures of mystery proteins. Four members of an archaea-only family, UPF201, resembled RNA-binding proteins in shape. The structures give the first clues to what these unknown proteins do.
plos-pone-0004003: In 2008, Gross, Busse, and Riemenschneider found a gene variant predicting chemo harm. A common DPYD polymorphism strongly raised the risk of severe fluoropyrimidine side effects. Patients carrying the variant suffered toxic reactions to normally safe chemotherapy doses. Screening for the variant before treatment could spare vulnerable patients from dangerous chemo.
plos-pone-0004103: In 2008, Sano, Miyaji-Yamaguchi, and Tsutsui found a gene switch for neurons. Topoisomerase II-beta switched on neuronal genes silenced in AT-rich genome zones. The enzyme opened locked regions late in nerve development. The mechanism links DNA shape to brain building.
plos-pone-0004203: In 2009, a Danish team compared protein shape-shifters. New similarity scores rated protein ensembles by shape and flex. The metrics captured how structures bend and change. The scores aid studies of function and evolution. The neat toolkit standardizes comparing floppy proteins.
plos-pone-0004303: In 2009, Cameron and Foster linked a pesticide to mouse breast tumors. Dieldrin exposure around birth and nursing altered mammary tumor growth in Her2/neu mice. The organochlorine's early hit shifted later cancer risk. The finding flags developmental pesticide danger for infants.
plos-pone-0357103: A chemical tag called β-hydroxybutyrylation may reshape genes in failing hearts. This paper integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics to reveal its association characteristics with heart failure. The combined analysis pinpoints which cells and genes the tag touches — a new layer in heart failure biology.
plos-pone-0357303: RSV isn’t just a children’s virus — it hospitalizes older adults too. This retrospective analysis of Brazil’s surveillance database measured the burden of RSV hospitalizations among adults aged 60 and older from 2013 onward. The numbers make the case for protecting seniors with vaccines and awareness, not just infants.
plos-pone-0353503: Comparing Chinese handwriting is hard: thousands of characters, endless personal styles. This paper built character-level attention Siamese networks that learn to judge whether two handwriting samples match. The model gives forensic examiners and archivists a tireless AI second opinion on questioned documents.
plos-pone-0358103: Reading emotions in text is big business — and accuracy is everything. This paper optimized sentiment classification with improved Senti-BERT plus BiLSTM-Attention. The hybrid architecture squeezes more accuracy from the models that decide whether a review glows with praise or grumbles with complaint.
plos-pone-0357203: When medical errors harm patients, the clinicians involved become ‘second victims’ — traumatized and often unsupported. This scoping review mapped the repercussions of the second victim phenomenon on healthcare workers. The synthesis shows what these hidden victims endure and which support actually helps them recover.
plos-pone-0357803: Acne does more than scar skin — it can seed phobic anxiety that outlasts the pimples. This study at a national dermatology hospital in Vietnam measured the prevalence, clinical phenotype, and associated factors of phobic anxiety disorders among acne patients. The findings firmly link dermatology with mental health.
plos-pone-0357903: Pneumococcus still colonizes children’s noses even in the conjugate vaccine era. This Brazilian cross-sectional study measured nasopharyngeal carriage of Streptococcus pneumoniae in children aged two to five in Salvador. The carriage data track the vaccine’s real-world impact — and its limits.
plos-pone-0352103: Do liberals and conservatives express political hatred differently? This paper tested within-person effects of political attitudes on outgroup animosity, uncovering a clear Democratic-Republican asymmetry. The evidence complicates the lazy both-sides narrative with careful longitudinal data.
plos-pone-0357403: After local extinctions, mite communities on grasslands reassemble — but how, and how fast? This paper tracked the fine-scale recovery of mite communities following local extinctions. The recovery patterns reveal the hidden rules of recolonization, informing grassland restoration everywhere.
plos-pone-0356103: Methamphetamine ravages the heart, driving inflammation in cardiac tissue. This rat study tested whether endurance training reduces those inflammatory markers in meth-exposed hearts. The results suggest exercise might partially undo the drug’s cardiac damage — a hopeful lead for recovery programs.
plos-pone-0354703: Trigraphene nanosheets — three atomic layers of carbon — fail in direction-dependent ways. This molecular dynamics study probed their anisotropic fracture mechanisms and crack-mediated mechanical degradation. The atomic-scale insights guide engineers designing with these remarkable materials.
plos-pone-0357003: Tomorrow’s Sudanese doctors need solid TB knowledge today. This cross-sectional study assessed tuberculosis-related knowledge, attitudes, and self-reported preventive practices among medical students at the University of Khartoum. The educational diagnosis reveals exactly where the curriculum must improve.
plos-pone-0356003: Sub-Saharan Africa’s primary care systems must absorb chronic disease care — but how? This paper published a systematic review protocol on implementation strategies for integrating non-communicable disease care into primary healthcare. The planned synthesis will identify which integration strategies actually work in resource-constrained settings.
plos-pone-0355403: Chip seal roads need fog seal overlays that grip despite sandy contamination. This paper optimized a sand-containing fog seal overlay design using response surface methodology. The optimized formulation extends pavement life on roads that conventional seals would abandon.
plos-pone-0355603: Training text classifiers is expensive — unless you pick the most informative examples. This paper proposed a novel hybrid model for identifying the most informative instances for improving text classification. The smart sampling slashes labeling costs while boosting model performance.
plos-pone-0354103: Surgically restoring blood flow to a starving brain — revascularisation — promises recovery but needs rigorous study. This paper published the protocol for a single-arm interventional study of hemodynamic, neurological, and cognitive outcomes after surgery for occlusive cerebrovascular disease. The planned research will quantify what revascularisation truly restores.
plos-pone-0353903: Mexican older adults’ intrinsic capacity — what their bodies and minds can do — reflects social vulnerability. This paper drew on the 2021 Mexican Health and Aging Study to examine those health determinants. The findings link social conditions to biological aging — demanding policies that address both.
plos-pone-0355503: The Changshan waterway — how many vessels can it safely pass? This paper researched its vessel passing capacity. The capacity analysis informs the shipping schedules and infrastructure investments that keep this aquatic artery flowing.
europmc-pmc2821003: Blue-green algae blooms release microcystins, toxins that poison animal cells. This 2010 paper reviews the molecular mechanisms behind microcystin toxicity. The authors explain how the toxins disrupt cells from the inside. The review matters because algal blooms are growing more common, threatening drinking water and wildlife alike.
europmc-pmc2880003: Word frequency lists power language research, and Chinese needed one from real speech. This 2010 paper builds SUBTLEX-CH from film subtitles, giving Chinese word and character frequencies. The authors' list reflects everyday language. Their resource became a standard for Chinese psycholinguistics.
europmc-pmc2893603: Combining genome studies boosts power, and this 2010 paper offers the software. The authors present GWAMA for pooling genome-wide association studies. Their tool streamlined multi-study number-crunching. The software became a workhorse of the GWAS era, behind many gene finds.
europmc-pmc2953403: Shell-derived materials may rebuild bone. This 2010 review surveys chitosan composites for bone tissue engineering. The authors weigh a natural scaffold's promise for implants. Their overview guides implant design choices. Surgeons eye these scaffolds for tricky fractures. The review compares blends, strengths, and cell response.
europmc-pmc2982803: Gut germs mirror ape family trees. This 2010 paper shows the gut germs of wild apes match their hosts' family tree. The authors reveal long co-evolution. Their work ties gut germs to host history. Each ape species keeps its own germ crew.
europmc-pmc2992503: Losing teeth shrinks quality of life. This 2010 review links tooth loss to daily well-being and mouth health. The authors' pooling puts numbers on the cost. Their work backs dental care for all. Chewing, smiling, and speaking all suffer. Dentures restore more than just looks.
europmc-pmc2998703: Missing data plagues survival studies, and this 2009 paper offers a fix. The author shows how to fill gaps in Cox model inputs. Their method rescues incomplete patient datasets. The work became a stats staple. Trial analysts use it when records go missing.
europmc-pmc3077403: Baby brains got growth atlases. This 2011 paper maps infant brains from birth to age two. The authors' atlases guide development studies. Their resource aids pediatricians. Rapid growth shows up month by month. Doctors spot delays against the maps. The atlases are free for researchers.
europmc-pmc3084703: A viral snippet splits proteins cleanly. This 2011 paper shows a 2A peptide from pig virus cuts cleanly in human cells, fish, and mice. The authors' tool spread through labs. It powers multi-gene builds. One gene in, several proteins out.
europmc-pmc6506903: In hospitals, "moral distress" describes what caregivers feel when they know the right thing to do but are blocked from doing it - a common strain on nurses and doctors. Yet the term gets used loosely, so its exact meaning has blurred. These authors combed through the research literature to pin down a sharper definition, spelling out the conditions a situation must meet to count as genuine moral distress.
europmc-pmc6509403: Excess weight does more than strain the body - it may age the brain. In mice, obesity pushed brain cells into a worn-out, inflammatory state called senescence, which the study links to anxious behavior and slower growth of new brain cells. Clearing those worn-out cells reversed the effects, suggesting a new path for treating anxiety and mood problems tied to obesity.
europmc-pmc6524403: Identifying a virus from raw sequencing data used to require bioinformatics expertise. Genome Detective is a free web tool that automates the job: it assembles viral genomes from high-throughput sequencing reads and names the pathogen. Clinics and labs can upload data and get fast, accurate identifications - useful for outbreak response and routine diagnostics alike.
europmc-pmc6527603: Mitochondria wear out with age, and renewing them may be a route to healthier aging. This review focuses on two control switches - Nrf2 and PGC-1alpha - that drive the birth of new mitochondria. Their interplay keeps the cell's power plants fresh; when the system falters, energy and resilience fade. Boosting these pathways is an active target in longevity research.
europmc-pmc6547503: Testing thousands of hypotheses at once - as in genomics - guarantees some flukes will look real. This practical guide walks computational biologists through methods that control the false discovery rate: which tool fits which study, and the traps that snag beginners. Clear examples and plain advice make a dry statistical topic genuinely usable.
europmc-pmc6586903: Microbiome studies usually report percentages - but percentages lie when total germ counts shift. This paper sets measurement standards using reference frames: a principled way to track which microbes truly rise or fall without laborious absolute counting. The method steadies a field long rocked by statistical controversy.
europmc-pmc6680503: Metabolomics machines spit out thousands of mystery molecules - naming them is the hard part. MolNetEnhancer stitches together molecular networking and annotation tools to group unknowns into chemical families. The combined pipeline turns raw spectra into interpretable maps of a sample's chemistry.
europmc-pmc6734003: RNA wears chemical decorations - and reading them in their natural state was impossible. This study used direct RNA sequencing to spot m6A modifications in native sequences, no copying or amplifying needed. The method opens the epitranscriptome to honest, unedited inspection.
europmc-pmc6734503: Breast tumors snuggle into fat - and the fat talks back. Cancer-associated adipocytes feed neighboring cancer cells with fuel and signals that spur progression. This review details the crosstalk: how fat cells become accomplices in breast cancer. The chatter suggests new targets beyond the tumor itself.
gao-gaoreports-b-310003: A 2007 GAO ruling settling two linked contract fights from Doyon-American Mechanical, JV and NAJV, LLC. Both firms said the agency's pick was flawed; the ruling weighs each claim and hands down the call. For builders chasing federal work, rulings like this one spell out the rules of fair play — and what sinks a bid.
gao-gaoreports-b-309803: A 2007 GAO ruling on a contract fight from Integrated Concepts & Research Corporation. The tech firm said the agency's research-deal award was off; the ruling tests the claim and calls the winner. For labs and tech shops chasing federal research dollars, the call shows how GAO scores a bid in the brainy end of the market.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1103: Arms flowing to allies on fast-track exemptions — GAO's 2007 report says the Pentagon's hall passes needed clearer ink and harder looks. The exemptions skipped full license reviews, and GAO found the safety catches loose. The findings weigh speed for friends against the risk of hot tech wandering astray.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-403: Floods, quakes, and storms kept coming in 2007 — and GAO's report says the nation's hazard homework was scattered. Plenty of mitigation efforts existed, but no joined-up federal game plan. The findings call for one coherent playbook against the disasters everyone knows are coming.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-703: Pension foxes were guarding the henhouse in 2007 — GAO's report says conflicts of interest around risky and failed plans challenged enforcement badly. The findings expose the tangled loyalties in the system. The report demands cleaner hands on the wheel of workers' retirements.
gao-gaoreports-b-308603: Presidential signing statements met the budget law in this June 2007 GAO ruling — what did the 2006 spending acts' add-on statements legally do? The call parses the constitutional tug-of-war over the purse. The ruling is fiscal law at its most dramatic: Congress, the President, and the meaning of a signature.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-203: The bankruptcy counseling mandate was an article of faith in 2007 — GAO's report again finds no proof that the required classes helped debtors at all. The findings repeat the doubt from before. The report's verdict stands: feel-good rules need evidence, not just feelings.
openalex-w7208836903: Potassium sorbate is a preservative found in many packaged foods, and this Brazilian toxicology study asks how safe it really is. Researchers tested both the pure chemical and common commercial formulas on rodents, checking short-term poisoning, longer-term organ effects, DNA damage, and blood chemistry. The paper compares pure sorbate against the mixtures sold to food makers, adding safety data on an additive most shoppers never think about.
openalex-w7128495003: A 77-year-old woman's weakening legs and weight loss puzzled her doctors. This case report untangles polymyositis from inclusion body myositis, two muscle diseases that mimic each other, after statins muddied the picture. The authors detailed the diagnostic work. A neurology case of look-alike diseases.
pmc-13455103: A 2026 materials informatics paper introducing electronegativity-inspired multidimensional representations for modeling chemical environments in materials. Borrowing the concept of electronegativity gives machine-learning models a more chemically sensible way to describe atoms in solids. Better representations mean better predictions of material properties.
pmc-13428703: A 2026 orthopedic study finding that operative treatment of lateral compression type 1 pelvic fractures increased from 2003 to 2018. These fractures were traditionally managed without surgery, so the trend marks a real shift in practice. The paper documents the change and invites scrutiny of whether it's justified.
pmc-13401703: A 2026 software paper presenting DDIapp, a web-based application for static drug-drug interaction assessment. Predicting interactions before they happen in patients is a core pharmacy task. The app makes the calculations accessible through a browser.
pmc-13486803: A 2026 phase 2 study of WT1 peptide vaccines as post-transplant maintenance immunotherapy for pediatric acute leukemias after allogeneic stem cell transplant. Keeping leukemia from returning after transplant is the goal. The trial tests the vaccine's safety and signal of efficacy.
pmc-13454703: This 2026 (listed 2025) in silico study linked broad environmental adaptation to root anatomical phenotypes in maize landraces. Root structure underpins drought tolerance. The computational analysis guides breeding.
pmc-13423803: A 2026 agricultural paper on insect farming by-products as a novel sustainable biofertilizer for crops. Bug waste becomes plant food. The circular economy angle is the appeal.
pmc-13531503: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of treatment duration's impact on opioid analgesia effectiveness. Longer isn't always better. The duration analysis informs prescribing.
pmc-13530803: A 2026 conference paper on failure after medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction — a propensity-matched comparative analysis. The failure modes were compared. The paper identifies the risks.
pmc-13435003: This 2026 German-language paper studied the effectiveness of an intervention to reduce stigmatization of people with skin diseases among health and body-care professionals. The anti-stigma program was tested. The paper reports the effectiveness for German-speaking readers.
pmc-13529603: A 2026 dentistry paper on stepwise management of temporomandibular joint internal derangement — from conservative therapy to arthrocentesis with hyaluronic acid. The jaw joint's treatment ladder was laid out. The stepwise protocol is the guidance.
pmc-13501303: This 2026 software paper presented ViralQC — assessing completeness and contamination of predicted viral contigs. The viral genome quality check is the tool. The QC is the need.
pmc-13500203: This 2026 neuroscience paper showed premovement suppression of corticospinal excitability is modulated by reaction time task requirements. The motor system's pre-action quieting depended on the task. The modulation is the finding.
pmc-13490903: This 2026 microbiology paper analyzed mutations in dfr and sul genes in trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole-resistant E. coli. The resistance genetics were mapped. The analysis informs surveillance.
pmc-13522803: A 2026 immunology review on CD8+ stem cell-like memory T cells — unveiling their potential for next-generation vaccination strategies. The long-lived T cells could transform vaccines. The review is the prospectus.
pmc-13474003: This 2026 paper described values-led coordination — Connect Coordination Victoria establishing a state-wide network of family carer mental health and wellbeing connectors (the title is truncated). The network supported carers. The coordination model is the innovation.
pmc-13473703: In this 2026 paper, the wound-healing properties of Anchusa azurea (Italian bugloss) were explored via a nanoliposome-based approach. The plant's healing was nano-delivered. The exploration is the finding.
pmc-13523703: A 2026 chemistry paper on photoinduced reductive elimination from sulfur enabling unique synthetic valorization of sulfonamides. The light-driven sulfur chemistry was the innovation. The valorization expands synthesis.
pmc-13458403: This 2026 chemistry paper showed G-quadruplex DNA reprograms the photochemistry of CX-5461 toward radical-driven anticancer activity. The DNA structure switched the drug's mechanism. The reprogramming is the insight.
pmc-13458903: This 2026 cardiology editorial, "Beyond Wall Thickness," looked past hypertrophy's obvious measure. The commentary reframes cardiac assessment. The editorial is the perspective.
pmc-13437203: A 2026 response letter to a paper on precision medicine in pediatric thyroid care — moving beyond adult frameworks toward age-stratified risk assessment. The correspondence engages the debate. The response is the scholarly exchange.
pmc-13402103: A 2026 gerontology paper on roles of self-stigma and meaning in the relationship between age and loneliness — a perspective from gerotranscendence. The aging-loneliness link was reframed. The perspective is the contribution.
pmc-13400903: A 2026 chemistry paper extending cofactor-tethered nanomachines to complex multienzyme redox cascades in continuous flow. The molecular machines ran cascades. The extension is the engineering.
pmc-13560203: A 2026 quasi-experimental study of a PERMA-based intervention's efficacy on PTSD symptoms and well-being in newly qualified operating room nurses. The positive psychology intervention was tested. The efficacy is the finding.
pmc-13526803: In this 2026 deep-sea paper, multi-omics and cultivation revealed laminarin-degrading PVC bacteria in the deep sea. The ocean's carbohydrate degraders were found. The revealing is the microbiology.
pmc-13527103: A 2026 physics paper: high-field-stabilized reentrant superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelate thin films. The superconductivity returned under high fields. The reentrance is the quantum surprise.
pmc-13464403: A 2026 AI paper: PCA-enhanced deep features for Alzheimer's disease stage classification with EFMM. The hybrid model staged the disease. The enhancing is the accuracy boost.
pmc-13453003: This 2026 paper presented semi-automated monitoring of deviations from historical incidence trends for enhanced timeliness in cancer control. The surveillance was automated. The monitoring speeds response.
pmc-13521103: This 2026 paper presented a novel technique for pectoral enhancement performed during excisional gynaecomastia procedures. The combined chest surgery was detailed. The technique is the innovation.
pmc-13435903: A 2026 quantitative analysis of government health expenditure's impact on health outcomes in China — mediation and threshold effects. The spending-outcome link was modeled. The threshold effects inform policy.
pmc-13452203: In this 2026 cardiology commentary, the question was posed: health literacy or care redesign in atrial fibrillation? The debate was framed. The commentary is the perspective.
pmc-13592403: In this 2026 paper, remote-controlled release of nitric oxide was achieved by a plasmonic waveguide coated with metal-organic frameworks. The light-triggered NO delivery is the advance. The release serves therapy.
pmc-13522603: This 2026 quantum computing paper scaled the surface code on heavy-hex superconducting quantum processors. The error correction was scaled. The scaling is the fault-tolerance advance.
pmc-13424803: In this 2026 breast cancer paper, distinct transcriptomic features of tumor and stromal cells in direct contact were found in luminal and triple-negative cancers. The touching cells' gene expression was profiled. The features are the microenvironment insight.
pmc-13420303: In this 2026 case report, acute exacerbation of COPD occurred immediately after extubation following percutaneous nephrolithotomy. The post-surgical lung crisis was documented. The case warns anesthesiologists.
arxiv-2606-16303: Steering a rig live while minding hard caps — say, a bot arm that must not twist past its stops — is a tough old nut. This paper trains a net pilot steered by slope-math (adjoints) that flies true and cheap, caps kept. For live-control builders.
arxiv-2606-16603: AI agents that analyze data can make consequential mistakes with no way to check their work. VeriGraph pushes toward verifiable data-analytic agents: systems whose analyses come with checkable guarantees. The paper presents the approach for researchers who need analytics AI that can prove what it claims.
arxiv-2606-16803: Cells decide their fate with genetic 'toggle switches' — circuits that flip between two states. This paper shows cell division itself changes those fate decisions: splitting the cell reshuffles the switch. It is a systems-biology paper for researchers modeling how cells choose identities.
